messages:
Daniel Reed: Hey team — quick one. My baby was born in Toronto on 2026-04-05. Im on Redwoods Canada payroll (Toronto entity) but currently still enrolled in the US medical plan. Can I add the newborn to our US benefits? What docs are acceptable (Canadian birth record only right now) and can coverage be retro to the birth date? Any payroll/tax catches I should expect moving between CA and US payrolls?
Tara Singh: Congrats Daniel! Birth is a QLE — you have 30 days from the birth to request. Carriers will accept a Canadian birth certificate or provincial birth registration as interim proof. SSN can be added later.
Daniel Reed: Nice. If I enroll now, will premiums be charged on my Canadian payroll or the US payroll? Im paid in CAD through Toronto.
Global Mobility: Good question. Since youre paid on the Canada entity, premiums will typically be handled via local payroll (CAD) for enrollments added while on the Canada employment track. Well coordinate benefits enrollment coding so carriers bill the right payroll. If you later switch to US payroll well reconcile any proration.
Daniel Reed: What about HSA/FSA? I have an HSA on the US plan. Does the child qualify for HSA coverage while Im on Canadian payroll?
Tara Singh: HSA contributions are US-tax-advantaged and generally require US-taxable wages to get the pretax benefit. You can have the child on medical coverage, but HSA pretax contributions from Canadian payroll typically arent allowed. Dependent care FSA is similar. Well flag Global Mobility so they can confirm exact treatment for your situation.
Daniel Reed: Will payroll retro deductions be applied back to 2026-04-05 if I submit within 30 days? Im trying to avoid a surprise large deduction.
Payroll Bot: If the carrier accepts retro effective date, premiums are prorated back to the effective date and will be deducted on the next Canada payroll run. We try to minimize surprises by splitting larger deductions across upcoming runs when possible — People Ops/Payroll will notify you before any deduction.
Daniel Reed: I only have the provincial birth registration PDF and a hospital record. No SSN yet. Also concerned about ID cards mailing to the US address while Im in Toronto.
Tara Singh: Those docs are fine to start. SSN can be added later. For ID cards: carriers can issue e-cards via their mobile apps, or we can request shipping to your US address with a note to hold until youre back. Put preferred mailing instructions in the portal upload comment.
Daniel Reed: Where do I upload the birth docs?
Tara Singh: Use the benefits portal > Add dependent (QLE) > Birth (international). Link: https://benefits.redwood.example/upload. Choose "Canada/International" in the dropdown and note your payroll as Toronto in the comments.
Daniel Reed: Uploaded files: onprov_birth_040526.pdf, hospital_record_040526.jpg. Marked payroll: Toronto.
People Ops Bot: Ticket #BP-8214 created for Daniel Reed. People Ops will review within 1 business day.
Tara Singh: Ill submit the enrollment request today and request carrier e-card access. If carriers reject retro effective date due to cross-border rules well propose the carriers earliest allowed date and explain payroll impact. Expect confirmation email and payroll note by EOD tomorrow.
Daniel Reed: Thanks all, appreciate the quick help! :pray:
